examples.ko: 허리가 잘록해서 이 원피스가 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: Her waist is narrow, so this dress suits her well.
This bottle is shaped so that it narrows in the middle.
An hourglass has a shape that is pinched in the middle.
That island is narrow in the middle.

examples.ko: 잘록한 허리선을 강조하는 옷이 요즘 유행이에요.
examples.en: Clothes that emphasize a slim waistline are in fashion these days.

examples.ko: 산 가운데가 잘록했던 곳에 작은 마을이 있었어요.
examples.en: There was a small village where the mountain narrowed in the middle.

explain: 허리나 병의 목처럼 가운데가 쏙 들어간 모양에 써요. 허리가 잘록하다는 말은 날씬하다는 칭찬으로도 자주 들려요. 반대로 가운데가 볼록하게 나오면 '불룩하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It describes a shape that is pinched in the middle, like a waist or the neck of a bottle. Saying someone's waist is 잘록하다 is often heard as a compliment about a slim figure. The opposite, bulging out in the middle, is '불룩하다'.

en: guess wrong; misjudge; make a miscalculation

examples.ko: 원인을 잘못 짚어서 문제가 더 커졌어요.
examples.en: We misjudged the cause, so the problem got bigger.
I guess I got the wrong person.

examples.ko: 의사가 병의 원인을 잘못 짚으면 치료가 늦어져요.
examples.en: If a doctor misjudges the cause of an illness, treatment is delayed.
I guessed the wrong direction and walked for a long time.

examples.ko: 상대의 속마음을 잘못 짚지 않도록 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful not to misread the other person's true feelings.

examples.ko: 이번 선거 결과는 다들 잘못 짚었어요.
examples.en: Everyone got the result of this election wrong.

explain: 짐작이나 판단을 했는데 틀렸다는 결과까지 담긴 말이에요. 원인, 방향, 상대의 마음처럼 '짚어 볼' 대상이 목적어로 와요. 비슷한 말로 '헛짚다'도 있어요.
explain_en: It already carries the sense that your guess or judgment turned out wrong. The object is something you try to pinpoint, such as a cause, a direction or someone's feelings. '헛짚다' is a similar word.

examples.ko: 우리 아이는 잠귀가 밝아서 작은 소리에도 깨요.
examples.en: My child is a light sleeper and wakes up at even small sounds.

examples.ko: 잠귀는 사람마다 달라서 같은 방에서도 누구는 깨고 누구는 안 깨요.
examples.en: Sensitivity to sound in sleep differs by person, so in the same room one wakes and another doesn't.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 잠귀가 어두워서 알람 소리를 못 들어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling sleeps so deeply that they can't hear the alarm.

examples.ko: 잠귀 밝은 고양이 때문에 밤에 자주 깨요.
examples.en: I often wake up at night because of my light-sleeping cat.

examples.ko: 엄마는 잠귀도 밝으시고 새벽에 일찍 일어나세요.
examples.en: My mom is a light sleeper and gets up early at dawn.

examples.ko: 잠귀가 너무 밝아서 이웃집 소리까지 들려요.
examples.en: I'm such a light sleeper that I can even hear the neighbors.

explain: 잠든 상태에서 소리를 알아듣는 정도를 말해요. 소리에 잘 깨면 '잠귀가 밝다', 잘 안 깨면 '잠귀가 어둡다'로 짝을 이뤄요. 깨어 있을 때 귀가 잘 들리는지와는 달라요.
explain_en: It refers to how well you pick up sound while asleep. Waking easily is '잠귀가 밝다' and not waking easily is '잠귀가 어둡다', a natural pair. It is different from how well you hear while awake.

examples.en: The detectives did a stakeout all night.

examples.ko: 오늘은 아침부터 잠복근무 중이라 연락이 어려워요.
examples.en: I'm on a stakeout since this morning, so it's hard to reach me.
After a long stakeout, they finally caught the culprit.
During the stakeout I ate nothing but cup noodles.
As the stakeout dragged on, everyone got very tired.

examples.ko: 잠복근무 때문에 가족 모임에 못 갔어요.
examples.en: I couldn't go to the family gathering because of a stakeout.

explain: 경찰이 범인을 잡으려고 숨어서 기다리며 하는 일을 말해요. 뉴스나 드라마에서 자주 나오고 '잠복근무를 하다'로 써요. 일반 직장 일에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is the work police do when hiding and waiting to catch a suspect. It often appears in news and dramas, as in '잠복근무를 하다'. It is not used for ordinary office jobs.

examples.en: This illness has an incubation period of about a week.
There are almost no symptoms during the incubation period.

examples.ko: 잠복기를 지난 뒤에 갑자기 열이 났어요.
examples.en: After the incubation period passed, I suddenly ran a fever.

examples.ko: 감염자가 잠복기에도 다른 사람에게 옮길 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can an infected person pass it on even during the incubation period?
How many days is the incubation period of the flu, usually?

examples.ko: 잠복기 동안 조심하라고 병원에서 말해 줬어요.
examples.en: The hospital told me to be careful during the incubation period.

explain: 병균이 몸에 들어온 뒤 증상이 나타나기 전까지의 기간이에요. '잠복기가 길다/짧다'처럼 말하고, 병원 안내나 뉴스에서 자주 들려요. 증상이 시작된 뒤의 기간에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is the period after germs enter the body and before symptoms appear. You say things like '잠복기가 길다/짧다', and it is common in hospital notices and the news. It is not used for the time after symptoms have started.

examples.ko: 아이가 잠잠히 앉아서 그림을 그리고 있어요.
examples.en: The child is sitting quietly and drawing a picture.

examples.ko: 바람이 잠잠히 가라앉을 때까지 기다려 보세요.
examples.en: Try waiting until the wind calms down.

examples.ko: 그는 아무 말 없이 잠잠히 듣고만 있었어요.
examples.en: He just listened quietly without saying a word.

examples.ko: 잠잠히 지내다 보면 소문도 곧 사라질 거예요.
examples.en: If you keep quiet, the rumor will fade soon too.

examples.ko: 화가 났는지 동생은 방에서 잠잠히 있어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling must be upset and is staying quiet in the room.

examples.ko: 회의 내내 잠잠히 있다가 마지막에 한마디 했어요.
examples.en: I stayed quiet throughout the meeting and said just one thing at the end.

explain: '잠잠하다'에서 나온 부사로, 소리나 움직임 없이 조용한 모습을 말해요. 사람이 말없이 있을 때뿐 아니라 바람, 소문이 가라앉았을 때도 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '가만히'나 '조용히'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: This adverb comes from '잠잠하다' and describes staying calm without noise or movement. It is used for a person staying silent and also for wind or rumors dying down. In daily talk people more often say '가만히' or '조용히'.

examples.ko: 이 선수는 잠재성이 커서 앞으로가 기대돼요.
examples.en: This player has great potential, so I look forward to the future.
The teacher believed in the students' potential.

examples.ko: 신기술의 잠재성은 아직 정확히 알 수 없어요.
examples.en: The potential of the new technology can't be known exactly yet.
The market's potential is big too, but there are risks.
We are looking for a writer with potential.
The results are still lacking compared with the potential.

explain: 겉으로 드러나지 않았지만 앞으로 나타날 수 있는 성질을 말해요. 말할 때는 '잠재력'이나 '가능성'을 더 자주 쓰고, '잠재성'은 글이나 설명에서 많이 보여요. 보통 '잠재성이 크다/높다/있다'로 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a quality that is not yet visible but may appear later. In speech people more often say '잠재력' or '가능성', while '잠재성' shows up in writing and explanations. It usually appears as '잠재성이 크다/높다/있다'.

en: potential; latent; within realm of possibility

examples.en: Please tell us about potential risks in advance.
This area has many potential customers.

examples.ko: 잠재적 문제를 먼저 찾아서 해결해야 해요.
examples.en: We need to find and solve potential problems first.
They are potential rivals for us.
We checked whether there were any potential threats.

examples.ko: 이 연구는 잠재적 가치가 아주 높아요.
examples.en: This research has very high potential value.

explain: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며서 '아직 드러나지 않았지만 생길 수 있는'이라는 느낌을 줘요. '잠재적인'이나 '잠재적으로'로도 자주 써요. 위험, 고객, 경쟁자 같은 말과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It modifies the noun after it, giving a sense of something not yet visible but possible. It is also commonly used as '잠재적인' or '잠재적으로'. It pairs well with words like risk, customer and rival.

examples.ko: 잠정적 결론이니까 나중에 바뀔 수 있어요.
examples.en: It is a tentative conclusion, so it may change later.
The company announced a provisional agreement.

examples.ko: 이 일정은 잠정적이라서 확정되면 다시 알려 드릴게요.
examples.en: This schedule is tentative, so I'll tell you again once it's confirmed.
We tentatively decided on next Friday.

examples.ko: 잠정적 휴업이니 곧 다시 문을 열 거예요.
examples.en: It's a temporary closure, so it will reopen soon.
That result is only provisional.

explain: 나중에 바뀔 수 있다는 뜻이 들어 있는, 임시로 정한 것에 써요. '임시'보다 딱딱해서 뉴스, 회의, 보고서에서 많이 나와요. '잠정 합의'처럼 '적' 없이도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is used for something set for now with the understanding that it may change later. It sounds more formal than '임시', so it appears often in the news, meetings and reports. It is also commonly used without 적, as in '잠정 합의'.

examples.ko: 아기가 잠투정을 해서 한참 안아 줬어요.
examples.en: The baby was fussy before sleep, so I held it for a long time.
It is hard to put a child to sleep when they are very fussy.

examples.ko: 우리 아들은 낮잠 자기 전에 꼭 잠투정을 부려요.
examples.en: My son always throws a fit before his nap.

examples.ko: 잠투정하는 아이에게는 조용한 노래가 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: A quiet song helps a child who is fussy about sleep.
Sleep fussiness usually decreases as children grow.

examples.ko: 동생이 잠투정 때문에 아침마다 짜증을 내요.
examples.en: My younger sibling gets cranky every morning because of sleep fussiness.

explain: 잠들기 전이나 잠에서 깰 때 어린아이가 괜히 울고 짜증 내는 것을 말해요. '잠투정을 하다/부리다'로 쓰고, 어른에게는 잘 쓰지 않아요. 어른이 잠이 덜 깨서 짜증을 낼 때는 다른 말로 풀어서 말해요.
explain_en: It means a young child crying or being cranky for no clear reason before falling asleep or on waking. You say '잠투정을 하다/부리다', and it is rarely used for adults. For a grumpy adult who is half asleep, people describe it in other words.

examples.ko: 시험 때는 잡념이 자꾸 생겨서 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: During exams stray thoughts keep popping up and I can't concentrate.

examples.ko: 잡념을 없애려고 조용히 숨을 쉬어 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried breathing quietly to clear my mind of stray thoughts.
While running, stray thoughts disappear too.

examples.ko: 잡념 때문에 책을 읽어도 내용이 들어오지 않아요.
examples.en: Because of wandering thoughts, nothing sinks in even when I read.

examples.ko: 잡념이 많은 날에는 일찍 자는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: On days with a lot of wandering thoughts, it's good to sleep early.

examples.ko: 청소를 하면 잡념에서 벗어날 수 있어요.
examples.en: Cleaning can help you get away from idle thoughts.

explain: 지금 하는 일과 상관없이 떠오르는 쓸데없는 생각을 말해요. '잡념이 들다/생기다/많다', '잡념을 버리다/없애다'처럼 써요. 걱정과 달리 꼭 불안한 생각이 아니어도 집중을 방해하는 생각이면 잡념이에요. '잡생각'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It means useless thoughts that come up and have nothing to do with what you are doing. It is used as '잡념이 들다/생기다/많다' and '잡념을 버리다/없애다'. Unlike worry, any thought that breaks your focus counts, even if it is not anxious. People also say '잡생각'.

examples.ko: 책상 서랍이 잡동사니로 가득 차 있어요.
examples.en: The desk drawer is full of odds and ends.

examples.ko: 창고에서 잡동사니를 정리하다가 옛 사진을 찾았어요.
examples.en: While sorting junk in the storeroom, I found old photos.
Before moving, I'd better throw away the clutter first.
This box has nothing but odds and ends in it.
There is so much clutter that the room looks small.

examples.ko: 가방 속 잡동사니 때문에 열쇠를 못 찾겠어요.
examples.en: I can't find my keys because of all the stuff in my bag.

explain: 쓸모가 있는지 없는지 애매한 자잘한 물건들이 뒤섞여 있는 것을 말해요. 완전한 쓰레기와 달리 아직 버리지 않고 모아 둔 물건이라는 느낌이 있어요. '잡동사니를 정리하다/버리다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It refers to small items of unclear use that are jumbled together. Unlike pure trash, it has a feel of things you have kept and not yet thrown away. It is often used as '잡동사니를 정리하다/버리다'.

examples.ko: 산길 양쪽에 잡목이 우거져서 걷기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: Brush grew thick on both sides of the mountain path, so it was hard to walk.
My father cut down scrub trees and used them as firewood.

examples.ko: 잡목 숲을 지나니 작은 계곡이 나왔어요.
examples.en: After passing through the scrubby woods, a small valley appeared.

examples.ko: 잡목들이 얽혀 있어서 길을 찾기 어려웠어요.
examples.en: The scrub trees were tangled, so it was hard to find the way.
They clear the scrub in advance to prevent forest fires.

examples.ko: 잡목 사이로 노루가 지나가는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a roe deer passing through the scrub trees.

explain: 소나무처럼 쓸모가 분명한 나무가 아니라 여러 종류가 섞여 자라는 자잘한 나무를 말해요. 주로 산이나 숲에서 '잡목이 우거지다', '잡목 숲'으로 써요. 한 종류의 나무를 가리키는 이름은 아니에요.
explain_en: It refers to small trees of mixed kinds growing together, rather than valuable trees such as pines. It is mostly used for mountains and forests, as in '잡목이 우거지다' and '잡목 숲'. It is not the name of one particular tree.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 잡무에 시달려서 정작 중요한 일을 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was bogged down in odd jobs all day and couldn't do the really important work.
New employees first learn the miscellaneous tasks.
There were so many chores that I worked overtime.

examples.ko: 서류 정리 같은 잡무는 제가 맡을게요.
examples.en: I'll take care of odd jobs like organizing documents.

examples.ko: 이 일 말고도 잡무를 여러 개 맡고 있어요.
examples.en: Besides this job, I'm handling several other small tasks.
I couldn't even eat lunch because I was dealing with odd jobs.

explain: 맡은 주요 일이 아닌 자질구레한 일을 말해요. 주로 회사나 학교 같은 사무 환경에서 쓰고, '잡무가 많다/밀리다'처럼 말해요. 집이나 현장의 허드렛일까지 넓게 말할 때는 '잡일'을 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It means small miscellaneous tasks that are not your main duties. It is used mostly in offices and schools, as in '잡무가 많다/밀리다'. For general odd jobs around the house or a work site, '잡일' is used more.

examples.en: Peddlers are not allowed to enter this building.
A peddler keeps ringing the doorbell, and it's annoying.
They are keeping peddlers out at the apartment entrance.

examples.ko: 지하철에서 잡상인에게 물건을 산 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I once bought something from a hawker on the subway.
The street is noisy because of the hawkers.
I put up a sign on the door saying no peddlers.

explain: 허락 없이 돌아다니거나 찾아와 물건을 파는 사람을 말해요. '잡상인 출입 금지', '잡상인 사절'처럼 안내문에서 자주 보여요. 조금 부정적인 말이라 상대방을 직접 부를 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It refers to people who go around or visit without permission to sell things. You often see it on signs such as '잡상인 출입 금지' and '잡상인 사절'. It has a slightly negative tone, so you wouldn't use it to address someone directly.

examples.en: Stop the nonsense now and just get to work.

examples.ko: 영상에 잡소리가 많이 섞여서 다시 찍었어요.
examples.en: The video had too much stray noise, so I filmed it again.

examples.ko: 옆 사람이 하는 잡소리 때문에 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: I can't concentrate because of the idle chatter next to me.

examples.ko: 잡소리를 늘어놓지 말고 핵심만 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't ramble on, just tell me the main point.
A lot of background noise got into the recording.
What nonsense are you talking about now?

explain: 쓸데없는 말이나 여러 가지 섞인 잡음을 말해요. 사람의 말에 쓰면 무시하는 말투가 되어서 윗사람에게는 쓰지 않아요. 기계에서 나는 소리는 '잡음'이 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It means pointless talk or mixed-in noise. When used about someone's words it sounds dismissive, so you don't use it toward superiors. For sounds from machines, '잡음' is more natural.

examples.en: Bears are omnivores, so they eat both meat and plants.
I eat anything, so there's no food I avoid.
Omnivorous animals adapt easily to their environment.
Pigs are animals that eat both meat and plants.

examples.ko: 책을 잡식으로 읽다 보니 관심 분야가 넓어졌어요.
examples.en: Reading all kinds of books has widened my range of interests.
Humans have a diet close to omnivorous.

explain: 고기도 식물도 다 먹는 식성을 말하고, '육식', '초식'과 짝이에요. 사람이 '나는 잡식이야'라고 하면 음식을 가리지 않는다는 뜻이에요. 책이나 영화를 분야 없이 두루 보는 것도 '잡식'에 빗대어 말해요.
explain_en: It describes a diet of both meat and plants, and pairs with '육식' and '초식'. When a person says '나는 잡식이야', it means they eat anything. People also jokingly use it for reading or watching all kinds of books and films.

examples.en: The police finally rounded up the fugitive.
The enforcement team is seizing illegal fishing boats.
Once they catch the culprit, the case will be over.
The police plan to bring in all the suspects.
The village only became quiet after the thief was caught.
They caught the thief and took him to the police station.

explain: 그냥 '잡다'보다 붙잡아서 데려오거나 가둔다는 느낌이 강해요. 경찰이나 단속 기관이 사람이나 불법 물건을 잡을 때 주로 써요. 일상에서 친구를 잡거나 물건을 쥘 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Compared with plain '잡다', it carries a stronger sense of catching someone and bringing them in or locking them up. It is mainly used when police or enforcement agencies catch people or illegal items. You would not use it for grabbing a friend or holding an object.

examples.en: It feels cool with my hair tied back.
I tied the boat to the post with a rope.

examples.ko: 짐이 떨어지지 않게 끈으로 단단히 잡아매세요.
examples.en: Tie the luggage tightly with a strap so it doesn't fall.

examples.ko: 자루 입구를 끈으로 잡아매고 나서 옮겼어요.
examples.en: I tied the mouth of the sack shut with string and then carried it.
I left the cow tied to a tree.
I tied my belt so tight that it's hard to breathe.

explain: 끈이나 줄로 단단히 묶어서 움직이지 않게 하는 것이에요. '묶다'보다 꽉 당겨 매는 느낌이 있어요. '머리를 잡아매다'처럼 머리카락을 묶을 때도 흔히 써요.
explain_en: It means to bind something firmly with a string or rope so it does not move. It feels more like pulling tight than plain '묶다'. It is also commonly used for tying up hair, as in '머리를 잡아매다'.

en: catch (a taxi or bus); hop on

examples.en: I hailed a passing taxi and went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 읍내에서 버스를 잡아타기 전에 점심을 먹었어요.
examples.en: I ate lunch before catching a bus in town.
I just caught the last bus and barely got home.
You can just hop on any bus at the stop.
I ran down the stairs to catch the subway.

examples.ko: 마침 오는 버스를 잡아탄 덕분에 늦지 않았어요.
examples.en: Thanks to catching a bus just as it came, I wasn't late.

explain: 오는 택시나 버스를 서둘러 바로 타는 모습을 말해요. 그냥 '타다'보다 급하게 잡아서 탄다는 느낌이 있어요. 택시, 버스, 막차처럼 길에서 타는 탈것과 자주 써요.
explain_en: It describes quickly hopping onto a taxi or bus that is coming. Compared with plain '타다', it feels like catching it in a hurry. It is often used for vehicles you board on the street, such as taxis, buses and the last bus.

examples.en: The rain ruined today's picnic.

examples.ko: 전화 한 통 때문에 기분을 잡쳤어요.
examples.en: One phone call ruined my mood.

examples.ko: 시험을 잡치면 다음 기회를 노려야 해요.
examples.en: If you botch the exam, you have to aim for the next chance.

examples.ko: 그 한마디가 분위기를 다 잡쳐 버렸어요.
examples.en: That one remark completely spoiled the mood.

examples.ko: 갑자기 정전이 되어서 저녁 모임을 잡치고 말았어요.
examples.en: A sudden blackout ended up ruining the dinner gathering.

examples.ko: 일을 잡치지 않도록 계획을 꼼꼼히 세워요.
examples.en: I make a careful plan so I don't mess up the work.

explain: 일, 기분, 분위기, 시험 같은 것을 망쳤을 때 쓰는 말이에요. '망치다'보다 구어적이고 거친 느낌이라 친구나 가까운 사이에서 많이 써요. 윗사람에게나 격식 있는 자리에서는 '망치다'가 더 안전해요.
explain_en: It is used when something like work, your mood, the atmosphere or an exam gets ruined. It is more colloquial and rougher than '망치다', so it is mostly used with friends and close people. With superiors or in formal settings, '망치다' is safer.

examples.en: My older brother finally got married at thirty.
My son has reached the age to marry.

examples.ko: 그는 이웃 마을 처녀에게 장가들었다고 해요.
examples.en: They say he married a girl from the neighboring village.

examples.ko: 장가들면 부모님 곁을 떠나는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people leave their parents' side once they marry.

examples.ko: 친구가 드디어 장가들게 되어서 축하해 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend is finally getting married, so I congratulated him.

examples.ko: 장가들기 전에 집부터 마련해야 한다고 해요.
examples.en: They say you should get a home before you marry.

explain: 남자가 결혼하는 것을 말하고, 여자가 결혼하는 것은 '시집가다'라고 해요. 요즘 일상에서는 '장가가다'나 그냥 '결혼하다'를 더 많이 써요. '장가들다'는 조금 옛스럽고 글에서 보이는 말이에요.
explain_en: It refers to a man getting married, while for a woman you say '시집가다'. In daily life today people more often say '장가가다' or simply '결혼하다'. '장가들다' sounds a bit old-fashioned and appears more in writing.

examples.en: At the meeting the department head went on and on at length.

examples.ko: 긴 장광설 끝에 결론은 한 줄뿐이었어요.
examples.en: After a long-winded speech, the conclusion was just one line.
Everyone got worn out by his long-winded talk.
Please stop the long speech and tell me the main point first.

examples.ko: 연설이 장광설로 끝나서 기억에 남는 게 없어요.
examples.en: The speech ended up so long-winded that nothing stuck with me.
As the long-winded talk continued, I got very sleepy.

explain: 길고 지루하게 늘어놓는 말이에요. 말솜씨를 칭찬하는 말이 아니라 '너무 길다'는 비판이 들어 있어요. 보통 '장광설을 늘어놓다/펼치다'로 써요.
explain_en: It means a long, tedious speech. It is not praise for fine speaking; it carries the criticism that something is too long. It is usually used as '장광설을 늘어놓다/펼치다'.

examples.ko: 저 아이는 체격이 좋아서 장군감이라는 말을 들어요.
examples.en: That child is well built, so people say he's general material.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 갓 태어난 손자를 보고 장군감이라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: My grandfather looked at his newborn grandson and said he'd make a great general.
He is so dependable that he seems like general material.
He wasn't general material, but he was a good soldier.
That friend has leadership, so he's general material.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 씩씩해서 장군감 소리를 들었어요.
examples.en: Since childhood I was spirited and got called general material.

explain: 몸집이 크고 기운찬 아이나 배짱 있는 사람에게 어른들이 덕담처럼 건네는 말이에요. '사윗감', '신랑감'처럼 '~감'이 붙으면 그 자리에 어울리는 사람을 가리켜요. '대통령감', '사장감'도 같은 방식이에요. 체격뿐 아니라 듬직한 성격과 리더십을 칭찬할 때도 써요.
explain_en: Adults use it as a kind word for a big, lively child or a bold person. As in '사윗감' and '신랑감', the ending 감 marks someone who suits a role, and '대통령감' and '사장감' work the same way. People also use it to praise a dependable character or leadership, not only a strong build.

examples.en: I sat down with my grandfather in front of the janggi board.

examples.ko: 공원에서 어르신들이 장기판을 둘러싸고 구경하고 있어요.
examples.en: At the park, elders are gathered around a janggi board watching.

examples.ko: 장기판 위에 말을 하나씩 놓아 보세요.
examples.en: Try placing the pieces on the janggi board one by one.
I bought a new janggi board and gave it to my father as a present.
In front of a janggi board, my father always becomes serious.

examples.ko: 이 장기판은 접이식이라서 들고 다니기 편해요.
examples.en: This janggi board is foldable, so it's easy to carry around.

explain: 장기를 두는 판이에요. 장기를 두는 것은 '장기를 두다'라고 하고, 바둑을 두는 판은 '바둑판'이라고 해서 짝으로 알아 두면 좋아요. 공원에서 어르신들이 두는 모습이 흔해요.
explain_en: It is the board on which janggi is played. Playing is '장기를 두다', and the Go board is '바둑판', a good pair to remember. A common sight is elders playing in a park.

examples.en: The economic slump has dragged on, so shops are struggling.
If the construction drags on, residents will be inconvenienced.

examples.ko: 이번 협상이 벌써 석 달째 장기화하고 있어요.
examples.en: This negotiation has already dragged on for three months.
It's hard to get a job because of the prolonged recession.

examples.ko: 문제가 장기화하지 않도록 빨리 해결해야 해요.
examples.en: We need to solve it quickly so the problem doesn't drag on.
They say the lawsuit may be prolonged.

explain: 어떤 일이나 상황이 오래 이어지게 되는 것을 말해요. 주어는 불황, 협상, 공사 같은 상황이고 뉴스에서 '장기화하다'와 '장기화되다'를 둘 다 많이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '길어지다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It means a situation or matter comes to continue for a long time. The subject is a situation such as a recession, negotiation or construction, and the news uses both '장기화하다' and '장기화되다'. In everyday talk, '길어지다' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 장난삼아 던진 말이 큰 싸움이 됐어요.
examples.en: A remark thrown out as a joke turned into a big fight.
I started it just for fun, and it became my job.
My friends teased me just for fun.
You shouldn't treat other people's promises like a game.

examples.ko: 그는 모든 일을 장난삼는 버릇이 있어요.
examples.en: He has a habit of treating everything as a joke.
It wasn't a joking act; I meant it.

explain: 진지하지 않게 놀이처럼 가볍게 하는 것을 말해요. 대부분 '장난삼아' 모양으로 쓰고, 뒤에 '던지다, 해 보다' 같은 말이 와요. '재미 삼아'와 비슷하지만 가볍게 다루는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It means doing something lightly, like a game, without being serious. It mostly appears as '장난삼아' followed by verbs like '던지다' or '해 보다'. It is similar to '재미 삼아' but has a stronger feel of treating something lightly.

examples.en: Don't play dangerous pranks on your friends.
The shop door got broken by the kids' mischief.

examples.ko: 남의 물건으로 장난질을 치면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't mess around with other people's things.
I don't know who pulled this kind of trick.
That's not a prank; it's a serious lie.

examples.ko: 장난질로 끝날 줄 알았는데 사고가 났어요.
examples.en: I thought it would end as a prank, but an accident happened.

explain: '-질'이 붙어서 장난을 나쁘게 보는 비난의 느낌이 있어요. 그냥 '장난'보다 못된 짓이나 속임수를 가리킬 때 많이 써요. '장난질을 치다/하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: The suffix -질 gives it a critical tone that looks down on the mischief. Compared with plain '장난', it is often used for nasty acts or tricks. It is used as '장난질을 치다/하다'.

examples.ko: 장년층을 겨냥한 건강 검진 상품이 최근 많이 나오고 있어요.
examples.en: Many health checkup packages aimed at the middle-aged group have come out recently.

examples.ko: 장년층 취업 지원 프로그램이 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A new job support program for middle-aged people has started.

examples.ko: 장년층은 운동 부족으로 건강이 나빠지기 쉬워요.
examples.en: Middle-aged people can easily lose health from lack of exercise.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 청년층보다 장년층이 더 많이 써요.
examples.en: More middle-aged people use this app than young people.
A large-print menu is convenient for middle-aged people.

examples.ko: 우리 동네는 장년층 인구가 점점 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: The middle-aged population in our neighborhood is gradually growing.

explain: 청년층과 노년층 사이의 나이대 사람들을 가리켜요. 정확한 나이 범위는 글이나 통계마다 달라서, '중장년층'이라고 묶어 말하기도 해요. 뉴스, 광고, 통계에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It refers to people in the age range between young adults and seniors. The exact age range varies by article or statistic, and people often group it as '중장년층'. It frequently appears in news, ads and statistics.

examples.en: Suddenly a downpour poured down, and my umbrella was useless.
The game continued even in the pouring rain.

examples.ko: 밤새 내린 장대비 때문에 길이 물에 잠겼어요.
examples.en: The road was flooded because of the downpour that fell all night.
I ran home through the pouring rain.
When the downpour stopped, the sky cleared up.
They say it will pour heavily in the afternoon.

explain: 장대처럼 굵고 세차게 내리는 비를 말해요. '장대비가 쏟아지다/내리다'로 자주 쓰고, 뉴스의 '폭우'보다 구어적이에요. 잠깐 내리는 '소나기'와 달리 비의 굵기와 세기를 강조해요.
explain_en: It refers to rain that falls thick and hard, like poles. It is often used as '장대비가 쏟아지다/내리다' and is more colloquial than the news word '폭우'. Unlike a short '소나기', it stresses the thickness and strength of the rain.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 장렬하게 패배했지만 박수를 받았어요.
examples.en: The player lost heroically but received applause.
Everyone remembers the firefighter's heroic sacrifice.

examples.ko: 장렬했던 마지막 경기를 잊을 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't forget that last, valiant game.

examples.ko: 그 장면이 너무 장렬해서 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: That scene was so stirring that I cried.
They were brave to the end, to the point you could call it heroic.

examples.ko: 그 선수의 장렬한 투혼에 관중이 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: The crowd applauded that player's heroic fighting spirit.

explain: 용감하고 기개가 있으면서도 비장한 느낌이 있어요. 희생이나 패배처럼 마지막까지 맞서는 장면에 어울리고, 일상 대화보다는 글에서 많이 보여요. 그냥 용감함을 말할 때는 '용감하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It conveys bravery together with a solemn, heroic tone. It suits scenes of sacrifice or defeat where someone resists to the end, and appears more in writing than in daily talk. For plain bravery, use '용감하다'.
